title: Interactive Transaction Bloat (Long-Running Locks)
pattern: Holding a database transaction open while executing non-database tasks (like network calls, file writing, or interactive client-side wait steps).
why_bad: The database transaction locks records (or tables) to ensure isolation. Blocking on network I/O (which can take hundreds of milliseconds or seconds) keeps database locks open excessively, freezing other concurrent transactions and causing lock escalation, timeouts, and severe tail latency.
detection: Look for calls to network I/O, heavy computational helper blocks, or non-database API methods executed between the statements starting and ending a database transaction.
counterexample: `Too subjective`. When working with highly restricted, low-concurrency internal administration databases where simplicity outweighs throughput.
source: *Martin Kleppmann - Designing Data-Intensive Applications (2017)*, Chapter 7, "Transactions" (Interactive multi-statement transactions, p. 244).
